question: What causes a React function component to render?
shortAnswer: Initial mount or a state update in the component or an ancestor.
strongAnswer: Rendering means React calling the component to compute UI. It happens on initial render via createRoot().render and when state updates with a set function. Parent renders typically cause children to render unless memoized.
advancedAnswer: Discuss that props are not a separate event stream; children render because reconciliation continues recursively after a parent render, and that render ≠ commit ≠ paint.
commonWrongAnswer: React re-renders only when props change via Object.is on every prop automatically without parent involvement.
